A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same underlying research, sharing authors, the compactness-and-margin loss, partial momentum, and several theoretical results. All pages, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison despite the substantial revision.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments on CIFAR10, SVHN, and RSCD, including accuracy tables, ablations, and feature visualizations in Section 7.

after.justification: v3 reports original clean and corrupted classification results on CIFAR10, SVHN, and a custom road dataset, alongside curvature analyses and feature visualizations.

M1.justification: v3 retains the original compactness, margin, and regularization objective as its clean-data branch, but adds a loss aligning noisy features with clean class centroids. Equations (12)–(13) introduce this additional training objective with lambda = 1. Partial momentum is retained; the noisy-feature constraint is an actual method addition.

E1.justification: CIFAR10 and SVHN remain, but the 27-class RSCD benchmark is replaced by a distinct custom dataset of 1,897 images covering dry, wet/watered, and icy/snowy roads. v3 also introduces Gaussian and uniform noise scenarios, occlusion, resolution degradation, stripe masking, and combined corruptions.

E2.justification: The CIFAR10/SVHN comparisons expand from standard softmax training in v2 to include noisy-only training, joint clean/noisy training, and stability training in v3 Tables 1–2. Normal training corresponds to the retained softmax baseline. The center-loss comparison in v2's RSCD Table 4 disappears with that experiment.

E3.justification: The retained ResNet experiments change the feature dimension from 30 to 128 and the main margin threshold from 6.0 to 5.0 (v2 Appendix F and Section 7.3; v3 Appendix H). Training-fraction evaluations are replaced by prescribed perturbation protocols. v3 additionally introduces an 80/20 custom-road split and evaluations on curvature-selected test subsets.

E4.justification: v2's component, margin-threshold, and momentum ablations are removed, including from the appendices. v3 adds corruption robustness studies, curvature–robustness correlations, curvature distributions, and loss-surface visualization. Intermediate-layer t-SNE analysis remains but now compares clean and noisy CIFAR10 features instead of clean CIFAR10 and SVHN features.

E5.justification: v2 provides point accuracies without repeated-run or uncertainty reporting. v3 systematically reports means and standard deviations over ten independent perturbations of fixed trained models (Tables 1–4 and Appendix H); deterministic resolution degradation uses one evaluation. It also introduces stochastic curvature estimation and Pearson correlations. These additions do not establish repeated training across seeds.

E6.justification: The training-fraction, ablation, and RSCD results are replaced by extensive robustness and curvature results. For example, v2 Table 3 reports 93.600% full-training CIFAR10 accuracy; v3 Table 1 reports 92.67% clean accuracy and 91.15 ± 0.20% at Gaussian noise 16/255. Changed model configurations and objectives prevent interpreting these as a same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: v3 adds definitions of feature/loss stability and Theorem 6.1 bounding input-loss curvature, with Gaussian-moment derivations and proofs in Appendix E. It removes v2's pairwise classification generalization theorem and its proof. The compactness generalization bound and intermediate-layer divergence theorem are retained as v3 Theorems 6.2 and 6.3, rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion shift from general classification accuracy and data efficiency to robustness while preserving clean accuracy. v3 adds central claims about class-level noisy-feature alignment, a bidirectional connection between Gaussian noise and input-loss curvature, and generalization to other corruptions. The earlier claim about matching full-data softmax performance using less training data is dropped.

C2.justification: v3 introduces explanations of the clean/noisy accuracy tradeoff, preservation of expressiveness through alignment by class, and robustness through curvature reduction. Section 6.1 qualifies the converse relationship as feature or loss stability under a small-gradient assumption. Section 7.2 acknowledges stability training's advantage on resolution degradation, while v2's margin-size and momentum tradeoff discussions disappear.

D1.justification: v3 documents curvature estimation using 20 Gaussian probes and step size 0.01, corruption parameters, custom-road preprocessing, and a new training recipe in Appendix H. The code destination changes from the margin_compact_loss GitHub repository to an anonymous robust_noise repository. Conversely, v2's explicit experimental centroid-momentum and regularization settings are not carried into v3's experimental specifications.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around noise injection, adversarial robustness, Lipschitz models, randomized smoothing, and curvature regularization, citing works such as Bishop, Zheng, Cohen, and Moosavi-Dezfooli. Several earlier contrastive-learning and discriminative-loss references disappear. Novelty is newly framed around connecting Gaussian training, input curvature, and robustness, while the shared center/margin foundations remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, experimental narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around robustness. Existing material is reorganized: decision boundaries move into Section 3, the squared-loss discussion moves from v2 Section 4.5 to v3 Appendix A, and retained theoretical analyses are consolidated within Section 6.

P2.justification: v3 adds method and feature-geometry diagrams, road-image examples, and corruption illustrations. Training-fraction and ablation plots are replaced by robustness and curvature displays; t-SNE panels are reconfigured for clean/noisy comparisons. Tables acquire noise-level columns and uncertainty entries, and the document template, headers, typography, and page layout change throughout.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful robustness controls, perturbation-level uncertainty, and mechanistic analyses, but removes v2's component/hyperparameter ablations and large-scale RSCD validation. Its central curvature proof also treats the quadratic approximation in Equation (14) as an equality in Appendix E without bounding the remainder, limiting support for the expanded theoretical claims. These substantive gains and losses leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
